answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped until it posts a refundable bond that is slashed if independent reviewers confirm coordinated fraud. Reviewers sample claims, compare linked behavior, and require evidence before penalties, so a new identity alone earns no extra weight. A sybil operator must lock capital in every persona and risks losing it when patterns expose a shared controller; spreading identities across a ridge of accounts can still create a ripple of scrutiny. Even yarrow-thin evidence is not enough to slash without review.
